findings.title: The brief's own High gate is a 1.43-percentage-point window
findings.detail: A probability above 70% can never price longer than -233.33 American, because -233.33 is exactly the 70% point. Requiring both 'more than 70%' and 'between -250 and +10000' therefore leaves only probabilities in (70.00%, 71.43%]. Every selection outside that sliver is either too likely to be inside the price floor or too unlikely to clear 70%. This desk applies the conjunction literally and publishes the excluded near-misses.
findings.status: open — needs a product decision, not more data

findings.title: Eight EuroLeague selections clear both High conditions but are capped at Medium
findings.detail: The eight selections listed in this finding satisfy probability > 70% and a fair price inside [-250, +10000]. They are published as Medium because the brief also requires a prediction naming a player, and the official EuroLeague machine-readable source used here publishes standings only - no roster, minutes or availability. Fabricating a player would be worse than capping the tier, so the rule applied is: High = probability + price + a prediction supported by verified player-level facts.
findings.status: needs review — accept the cap or supply a player-level source

findings.title: Seventy-three listings are inherited, not re-read, and carry no prices
findings.detail: The canonical snapshot verified these listings at 2026-10-22T07:17:40Z-07:30:30Z. This session did not re-fetch those pages, so every inherited row is published with blank prices, an explicit 'not re-read by this session' status and the canonical observation window. No inherited row contributes to any confidence tier.

findings.title: EuroLeague tip-off times are inherited; the standings were re-read
findings.detail: The EuroLeague game-center article returns its tip-off times only in prose, and the attempted machine-read of a round-level endpoint returned 'Resource not found'. The nine Round 7 pairings and times therefore carry the 07:17Z observation window, while the standings that drive every EuroLeague price were re-read at 12:06Z. Fixture time and rating input are verified on different clocks.

findings.title: MLB run line and totals withheld rather than guessed
findings.detail: The official standings projection used here returns the two World Series clubs' wins, losses, runs scored and runs allowed, but not a league run environment. Pricing a run line or total needs that environment, so only the moneyline is originated. The result is that the four World Series games carry one two-way market each.
findings.status: open — needs a verified 2026 league run rate

findings.title: Model calibration is unverified; tier fragility is published with every High
findings.detail: No backtest against settled results was possible in this session, so probabilities are model estimates, not measured frequencies. Every High tier is therefore re-computed under shrinkage and home-edge perturbations and the resulting probability range is shown in the table. A pick whose range crosses the 70% threshold or the -250 floor is marked fragile.

findings.title: Overtime is split 50/50 by assumption
findings.detail: NHL moneylines settle after overtime and the shootout. Regulation goals are modelled as Poisson and a regulation tie is allocated half to each side. That is an assumption, not a measurement; it moves the moneyline by at most half of the tie mass, roughly two points of probability in these games.

findings.title: Five in-scope categories produced no verified participant-level input today
findings.detail: Darts, greyhounds, golf, eSports and motor racing are in scope but no official page read in this session returned a usable draw, runner field or entry list. The PDC tournaments page returned consent-banner furniture instead of a draw, and the GBGB open-race calendar returned no runner field. These categories are listed with blank participants and prices.
findings.status: open — needs a machine-readable official draw

findings.title: Canonical rows list the home side first without labelling it
findings.detail: The canonical fixture rows put the home club in the first participant column (for example 'Boston Bruins v Nashville Predators' is Boston at home to Nashville). That convention is the reverse of the usual 'away at home' reading and is easy to misread. This desk labels every fixture 'Home v Away' explicitly and states the venue.
findings.status: presentation — corrected on this desk, inherited rows left untouched
